title: 1996 AHSME Problem 24
statement: The sequence \[ \begin{gathered} 1,2,1,2,2,1,2,2,2,1,2,\\ 2,2,2,1,2,2,2,2,2,1,2,\ldots \end{gathered} \] consists of \(1\)’s separated by blocks of \(2\)’s with \(n\) \(2\)’s in the \(n\)th block. The sum of the first \(1234\) terms of this sequence is

solutions.text: Through block \(k\) there are \(k\) ones and \(\frac{k(k+1)}{2}\) twos, hence \(\frac{k(k+3)}{2}\) terms. For \(k=48\) this is \(1224.\) Their sum is \[ 48+2\left(\frac{48\cdot49}{2}\right)=2400. \] The next \(10\) terms are one \(1\) and nine \(2\)’s, with sum \(19.\) The requested sum is \(2419,\) so the correct answer is B.
hints: Count the total number of terms through the end of the \(k\)th block
Find the last complete block before term \(1234\), then account for the partial next block
